commentary.source: Plain sense within the Vairagya Prakarana; Ananda Bodhendra's Tatparya Prakasha not consulted

claim: Craving alone reduces even the wise, brave and steady to a blade of grass in an instant.

heals.why: shows that craving lowers anyone, so being caught by it is no special failing

commentary.reading: From Rama's censure of trishna.
commentary.source: Plain sense within the Vairagya Prakarana; Ananda Bodhendra's Tatparya Prakasha not consulted

claim: The senses are the enemies; the self strikes the self, and the mind is the mind's own enemy.

depicts.why: the sense of being one's own worst enemy

commentary.reading: Rama's lament on inner enmity. Vasishtha's reply is that the same mind, by effort, lifts itself.
commentary.source: Plain sense within the Vairagya Prakarana; Ananda Bodhendra's Tatparya Prakasha not consulted

line_issue: 'No one hurts us like we hurt ourselves' is added and reads as blame. Suggested: 'Our own senses turn against us. The self strikes the self, and the mind becomes its own enemy.'

claim: Steadiness gives way, people keep rising and falling; bad company is easy to find and good company rare.

depicts.why: weariness at a world where nothing holds
good company is hard to come by

commentary.reading: From the closing sweep of Rama's lament.
commentary.source: Plain sense within the Vairagya Prakarana; Ananda Bodhendra's Tatparya Prakasha not consulted

claim: Only the awakened are happy: cool within, working for others' good and moved by others' pain.

cultivates.why: being moved by another's pain
working for others' good
a mind cool in itself

commentary.reading: Rama names the buddha, the awakened one, as the only happy person: inner coolness joined to active compassion.
commentary.source: Plain sense within the Vairagya Prakarana; Ananda Bodhendra's Tatparya Prakasha not consulted

claim: True heroes cross the ocean of body and senses with its waves of mind, more than the ocean of battle.

cultivates.why: mastery of one's own mind counted as true courage
riding out the waves of the mind

commentary.reading: Rama redefines shaurya as victory over mind and senses.
commentary.source: Plain sense within the Vairagya Prakarana; Ananda Bodhendra's Tatparya Prakasha not consulted

claim: Who can sleep at night after a day of wandering that held none of the good work the wise rely on?

depicts.why: lying awake after a busy day that held nothing of worth

commentary.reading: Rama on days wasted in restless movement without sadhu-karma.
commentary.source: Plain sense within the Vairagya Prakarana; Ananda Bodhendra's Tatparya Prakasha not consulted

claim: Those days, those great ones, that wealth and those deeds have all become memory; we too go in a moment.

depicts.why: everything once solid is seen as already memory
ache for what has passed

commentary.reading: Rama on universal change; in the text this insight is what makes him ready for teaching.
commentary.source: Plain sense within the Vairagya Prakarana; Ananda Bodhendra's Tatparya Prakasha not consulted

claim: No trouble of the mind fails to fade in the company of the noble-minded, as night's darkness fades before the moon.

heals.why: a way out is named: good company
one does not have to carry it alone

cultivates.why: trust in satsanga

commentary.reading: Rama ends his lament with hope in sat-sangama, later listed by Vasishtha as one of the four gatekeepers of liberation.
commentary.source: Plain sense within the Vairagya Prakarana; Ananda Bodhendra's Tatparya Prakasha not consulted

claim: How can a person live and act in the world and not be bound, like water on a lotus leaf?

depicts.why: the wish to stay engaged and yet free

commentary.reading: Rama's question, pointing to Janaka; the whole teaching answers it with jivanmukti, freedom while acting.
commentary.source: Plain sense within the Vairagya Prakarana; Ananda Bodhendra's Tatparya Prakasha not consulted

claim: Nothing on earth or in heaven is so trivial that the wise cannot make it delightful.

cultivates.why: a clear mind lends beauty to small things
delight does not depend on the size of the thing

commentary.reading: Rama's praise of the wise as he asks them for help.
commentary.source: Plain sense within the Vairagya Prakarana; Ananda Bodhendra's Tatparya Prakasha not consulted

claim: Tell me the method by which sorrow does not come to me while I carry on with life's work.

depicts.why: he asks for a workable way, not an escape
work as it is now brings sorrow

commentary.reading: Rama asks for a yukti for living and acting without sorrow; he is not asking to renounce.
commentary.source: Plain sense within the Vairagya Prakarana; Ananda Bodhendra's Tatparya Prakasha not consulted

claim: Whoever wants a thing and works for it step by step surely attains it, unless he turns back halfway.

heals.why: doubt about whether effort pays is answered flatly
the only failure named is stopping halfway

cultivates.why: steady effort in sequence
not turning back at the midpoint

commentary.reading: Vasishtha's doctrine of paurusha: rightly directed effort bears fruit; daiva is no separate force.
commentary.source: Plain sense within the Mumukshu Vyavahara Prakarana on paurusha; Tatparya Prakasha not consulted

claim: Effort is of two kinds, past and present, and past effort is quickly overcome by present effort.

heals.why: the past is real and is not the last word
what feels fixed is shown as movable

cultivates.why: today's effort is the stronger force
begin from where one stands

commentary.reading: What is called fate is one's own earlier action; present purushartha can defeat it, as a strong man defeats a weaker one.
commentary.source: Plain sense within the Mumukshu Vyavahara Prakarana on paurusha; Tatparya Prakasha not consulted

claim: Past and present effort fight like two rams and the weaker yields, so strive so that today's effort wins.

heals.why: the weight of the past is one contestant, not the judge

cultivates.why: make today's effort the stronger ram
strive by every sound means

commentary.reading: Daiva is only prior purushartha; the two contend and the stronger wins, so present effort should be made the stronger.
commentary.source: Plain sense within the Mumukshu Vyavahara Prakarana; Ananda Bodhendra's Tatparya Prakasha not consulted

claim: Past faults are certainly stilled by present virtues, as yesterday's fault is undone by today's good.

heals.why: a past mistake is not permanent; today's conduct answers it

cultivates.why: do the good thing today
repair is possible

commentary.reading: Vasishtha's assurance that prior dosha yields to present guna; the everyday example is offered as proof.
commentary.source: Plain sense within the Mumukshu Vyavahara Prakarana; Ananda Bodhendra's Tatparya Prakasha not consulted

claim: 'Fate drives me' is the talk of ruined minds; fortune turns away from those who look only to the unseen.

heals.why: fate as an excuse is taken away

commentary.reading: A teacher's sharp line against fatalism as an excuse for not trying; it is not aimed at losses no effort could prevent, which Vasishtha addresses at 2.6.21.
commentary.source: Plain sense within the Mumukshu Vyavahara Prakarana; Ananda Bodhendra's Tatparya Prakasha not consulted

claim: But for laziness, who would not be wealthy or learned? Through laziness the earth is full of the poor and dull.

heals.why: sloth is named as the great waste

commentary.reading: Hyperbolic censure of alasya in the praise of effort. Read literally it blames the poor for poverty; keep it out of general serving.
commentary.source: Plain sense within the Mumukshu Vyavahara Prakarana; Ananda Bodhendra's Tatparya Prakasha not consulted

claim: Fate is nothing but past effort; set it aside and lift yourself firmly through good company and good teachings.

heals.why: what seemed an outside decree is shown to be workable

cultivates.why: lift yourself
lean on good people and sound teaching

commentary.reading: Summary of the doctrine: daiva equals prior paurusha; the means of uplift are sadhu-sangama and sat-shastra.
commentary.source: Plain sense within the Mumukshu Vyavahara Prakarana; Ananda Bodhendra's Tatparya Prakasha not consulted

claim: As the effort, so the fruit; there is only effort, and what is called fate is that same effort.

cultivates.why: results are tied to effort, not to a hidden decree

commentary.reading: Restatement: paurusha alone exists; daiva is a name for it.
commentary.source: Plain sense within the Mumukshu Vyavahara Prakarana; Ananda Bodhendra's Tatparya Prakasha not consulted

claim: As people cry 'how painful' in pain, 'alas, fate' is only another word for the same cry.

heals.why: the word fate is seen as a cry of pain, not an explanation

commentary.reading: Vasishtha empties the word daiva of force: it expresses distress and names no real agent.
commentary.source: Plain sense within the Mumukshu Vyavahara Prakarana; Ananda Bodhendra's Tatparya Prakasha not consulted

claim: Present and past effort overpower each other by strength; it is always human striving, and the unagitated one wins.

heals.why: calm is named as the deciding factor in a long contest

cultivates.why: staying unagitated through setbacks
it is all one's own striving

commentary.reading: Anudvega, freedom from agitation, is what lets present effort prevail.
commentary.source: Plain sense within the Mumukshu Vyavahara Prakarana; Ananda Bodhendra's Tatparya Prakasha not consulted

claim: Do not grieve over wealth lost despite effort; where my strength has no power, lamenting is useless.

heals.why: loss beyond one's power is released from self-torment
not everything lost was a failure of effort

cultivates.why: effort where it works, acceptance where it cannot
telling the two apart

commentary.reading: The limit Vasishtha himself sets on the effort doctrine: what lies outside one's power, like death, is not to be wept over daily.
commentary.source: Plain sense within the Mumukshu Vyavahara Prakarana; Ananda Bodhendra's Tatparya Prakasha not consulted

claim: When the mind is sunk in the harmful, bring it by effort to the good; this is the gist of all teaching.

heals.why: drift is answered by one repeatable move

cultivates.why: turn the mind back each time
knowing harmful from helpful

commentary.reading: Called sarva-shastrartha-sangraha, the digest of all scripture: redirect chitta from ashubha to shubha by effort.
commentary.source: Plain sense within the Mumukshu Vyavahara Prakarana; Ananda Bodhendra's Tatparya Prakasha not consulted

claim: The eater is satisfied, the walker arrives, the speaker speaks; human effort bears fruit.

heals.why: nothing arrives for the one who does not move
